L9: ## Why refer your patients?

L5: 
L6: # Clinical Study for Cats with Mammary Cancer - Information for owners
L7: 
L8: ##
L9: 
L10: ## The care your cat will receive
L11: ### Standard surgical care
L12: 
L13: Your cat will undergo routine tumour removal, just like any cat receiving mammary gland surgery at our Veterinary Teaching Hospital.
L14: 
L15: ### Innovative therapy
L16: 
L17: In addition to standard treatment, your cat will receive the investigational therapy (GCN2-IN-6) that will need to be administered orally before and after the surgery.
L18: ### Close monitoring
L19: 
L20: Apart from you as an owner, veterinary specialists will follow your cat throughout the study to ensure their comfort, safety, and well-being.
L21: Preclinical studies at the Small Animal Department demonstrated that this therapy is well-tolerated by cats, with little to no side effects nor with any relevant changes in any blood parameter.
L22: 
L23: ## Benefits and Impact
L24: ### Potential benefit for your cat
L25: 
L26: Participation may help to lower the risk of tumour recurrence and/or tumour spread (metastasis).
L27: The novel drug will be supplied without any additional cost.
L28: 
L29: ### Advancing feline care
L30: 
L31: Your cat’s involvement contributes valuable information toward developing new cancer treatments to increase the life expectancy for cats.

L5: # Fluorescentie Levensduur Beeldvorming
L6: 
L7: Een nieuwe beeldvormingstechniek om chirurgen te begeleiden bij het verwijderen van kanker: Fluorescentie Levensduur Beeldvorming
L8: 
L9: (S. Janssen/H. de Rooster)
L10: 
L11: An English version of this information for owners/veterinarians can be found later in this document
L12: Honden en katten waarbij kanker in een vroeg stadium wordt vastgesteld krijgen vaak de optie chirurgie aangeboden. Dit blijft een van de beste mogelijke behandelingen voor kankerpatiënten waarbij nog geen uitzaaiingen worden waargenomen. Tijdens de chirurgie proberen chirurgen de volledige massa te verwijderen om de kans op recidieven te verkleinen.
L13: Omdat chirurgen tijdens heelkundige ingrepen aangewezen zijn op hun eigen zicht en tast, én ons zicht niet toelaat om alle kleine kanker cellen te detecteren, wordt er gezocht naar nieuwe technieken die chirurgen kunnen helpen. Er worden contrast stoffen ontwikkeld die als kleine gidsjes de kanker cellen zichtbaar maken die we niet met het blote oog kunnen zien. De contraststoffen doen dit door licht uit te zenden. Dat licht kan dan gedetecteerd worden met speciale camera systemen.

L19: # Centro de Oncologia Estima
L20: 
L21: 【3†Image】
L22: 
L23: O COE é coordenado pelo Prof. Dr. Lucas Rodrigues, que tem se dedicado ao tratamento dos pacientes oncológicos há mais de 15 anos. Este centro de referência oferece o que há de mais moderno no tratamento oncológico aos pets, combinando tecnologia diagnóstica, inovação terapêutica e toda a atenção e cuidado que os pacientes e toda a família precisam.

L28: 
L29: Reproduzir vídeo
L30: Por meio de parcerias com empresas de desenvolvimento e pesquisa, os pets têm acesso a novas alternativas no combate ao câncer, sempre focando no controle da doença e na quantidade de vida dos pacientes. O desenvolvimento de novas medicações passa por diversas etapas chamadas de ensaios pré-clínicos e pesquisa clínica (Clinical Trial).
L31: O COE é uma unidade do Estima Hospital Veterinário criada para a realização de estudos clínicos, regidos por regulamentação nacional e internacional de boas práticas clínicas. Estudo clínico é um conjunto de investigação para o desenvolvimento de novos medicamentos. Por meio dele avaliamos a segurança e eficácia de um novo tratamento.
L32: O estudo clínico permite que novos medicamentos sejam disponibilizadas para os pacientes, e os dados desse tratamento sejam utilizados cientificamente para comprovar a ação do mesmo.

L17: # New Cancer Treatments for Dogs
L18: 
L19: A cancer diagnosis can be difficult for any family. Understanding the available treatment options and deciding what may be right for your dog can feel overwhelming.
L20: 
L21: CaniVax is developing new cancer drugs and therapeutic vaccines for dogs, using advances in modern cancer science to create additional treatment options for canine patients.
L22: ## Dogs Deserve Better Cancer Treatment
L23: 
L24: Cancer is one of the most serious diseases affecting dogs. Surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and supportive care can make a real difference, but important gaps remain. For many canine cancers, treatment options become more limited when the disease returns, progresses or stops responding to therapy.
L25: This can leave families facing difficult decisions. A treatment may control the cancer for a time but not prevent it from returning. Other options may become less suitable as the disease advances, or as treatment burden and quality of life become increasingly important. For too many dogs, there simply are not enough good options available when they are needed most.

L4: 
L5: Pet owners often ask us if we are aware of any CLINICAL TRIALS that may be available to their cat or dog who has been diagnosed with cancer. L6: Each clinical trial has very specific qualifications for participation that include everything from the breed and age of the participant to the life expectancy, weight and of course the type of cancer. L4: ## Recrutement pour un essai clinique multicentrique pour le traitement par cimentation des ostéosarcomes appendiculaires chez le chien.
L5: 
L6: Les cliniciens du Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Vétérinaire d’Oniris et la société TheraVet ® réalisent actuellement une étude clinique prospective multicentrique sur le traitement de l’ostéosarcome du chien avec un ciment osseux injectable (BIOCERA-VET®).
L7: 
L8: ### Qu’est-ce que l’ostéosarcome ?
L9: #### 【4†Descriptif de la maladie】
L10: 
L11: L’ostéosarcome est le cancer des os le plus fréquent chez le chien, représentant 85% de tous les cancers osseux canins. Ce cancer, très agressif, est à l’origine de fractures pathologiques et de douleur aigüe. La durée de survie moyenne de l’animal sans traitement se situe entre 4 et 5 mois et moins de 10% des chiens atteints d’ostéosarcome survivent 1 an.

L0: # Trials clinici in Oncologia Veterinaria
L1: 
L2: Al fine di far progredire la conoscenza sulle malattie oncologiche che colpiscono i nostri animali da compagnia, i medici veterinari che operano presso l’Ospedale Veterinario dell’Università di Bologna conducono studi clinici volti a valutare l’efficacia di nuove indagini diagnostiche e strategie terapeutiche. Queste scoperte possono spesso essere applicate alla medicina in tutte le specie.
L3: La maggior parte delle ricerche condotte presso il nostro Ospedale si basa sull’applicazione clinica di protocolli innovativi e promettenti sulla base di dati preliminari ottenuti in laboratorio. L’inclusione nello studio consente al paziente di ricevere, a basso costo, un trattamento potenzialmente vantaggioso e superiore rispetto alla terapia attualmente disponibile, con risvolti positivi anche per i futuri malati.
L4: Tutti gli studi clinici sono avviati solo dopo il ricevimento di un parere favorevole da parte del Comitato Etico-Scientifico dell’Università.
L5: Il personale medico discute con il proprietario dell’animale i requisiti necessari all’arruolamento in uno specifico protocollo di ricerca, elencandone i vantaggi, i rischi e le opportunità per quel paziente specifico. In caso di inclusione nello studio, il proprietario provvede alla firma di un consenso informato alle indagini e ai trattamenti sul proprio animale.

L10: # 研究内容
L11: 
L12: 近年、犬や猫のがんによる死亡が大きな課題となっています。日本小動物がんセンターにも、多くのご家族が有効な治療を求めて来院されますが、発見時には既に進行していることが少なくありません。現行の獣医療だけでは、すべての進行がんを治癒に導くことは困難です。
L13: 
L14: どうぶつトランスレーショナルリサーチセンターでは、動物のがんに対する新しい治療法と、早期発見のための診断法の開発に取り組んでいます。基礎から臨床までをつなぐ研究を加速し、いま目の前で困っている動物たちに、一日でも早く有効な選択肢を届けることが私たちの使命です。

L8: # 臨床研究情報
L9: 
L10: ## 臨床試験について
L11: 
L12: 本院で行っている、もしくは行う予定の臨床試験についてです。臨床試験とは、安全で有効となりうることが期待される医薬品もしくは医療機器を用いた治療です。 飼い主様への十分な説明と、飼い主様の同意の下で実施します。現在実施している臨床試験は以下の通りです。
L13: 
L14:   * 【0†慢性腸症罹患犬に対する乳酸菌およびオリゴ糖の有効性に関する臨床試験】
L15:   * 【1†犬の組織球性肉腫に対する抗PD-1抗体を用いた臨床試験】
L16:   * 【2†犬猫の固形腫瘍に対するがんオルガノイドスクリーニング検査に基づく分子標的薬投与の安全性と有効性検証のための臨床試験】
L17:   * 【3†ネコの移行上皮癌に対するラパチニブの獣医師主導臨床試験】
L18:   * 【4†犬の膀胱・尿道移行上皮癌および前立腺癌に対する臨床試験】
L19:   * 【5†犬の膀胱癌に対するIDO1阻害剤の臨床試験】
L20:   * 【6†犬の固形腫瘍に対する高分子型抗癌剤の臨床試験】

L8: # Our Solution
L9: 
L10: Market Opportunity
L11: ## A One Health Opportunity
L12: 
L13: Cancer is one of the leading causes of death in dogs, and owners increasingly seek the same standard of care they would expect for a family member. Yet treatment options remain limited: surgery, chemotherapy and radiation are costly, not widely available, and rarely control cancer once it has spread.
L14: The same is true in people. Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide, and the lungs are a common site of metastasis. A therapy proven against lung metastases in dogs therefore addresses an unmet need in two species, through one programme.

L37: Los ensayos clínicos en oncología veterinaria son estudios que pueden asustar en un principio tanto al veterinario remisor del caso como a los dueños. L29: # Devoted to the Fight Against Canine Cancer
L30: 
L31: We seek to break the barriers of traditional cancer treatment. Through collaboration with colleagues and research scientists, we want to offer the most effective cancer treatment for canine B cell lymphoma.
L32: ## Why We Do It
L33: 
L34: Canine B cell lymphoma is a very prevalent cancer in dogs of all breeds. It behaves much like non-Hodgkin lymphoma in humans and much of the research has taken place with dogs. Aurelius Biotherapeutics is utilizing this information and applying it to canine lymphoma treatment.
L35: ## Canine Lymphoma Treatment
L36: 
L37: For the past decade, our team has concentrated on the treatment of canine B cell lymphoma using adoptive transfer of T cells, commonly referred to as ACT. Our sole focus is to deliver safe and effective adoptive T cell immunotherapy in the fight against cancer. By using the patients own T cells, we can enhance the immune system so it can recognize and fight the cancer cells more effectively.

L3: 【0†Image: image】
L4: 
L5: Benno Therapeutics – Advancing Cancer Care for Dogs
L6: 
L7: Cancer is one of the most common and devastating diseases in companion animals. An estimated one in four dogs will develop cancer during their lifetime, with risk increasing significantly in dogs over the age of six. Despite this high prevalence, treatment options often remain limited, burdensome, or ineffective, especially for aggressive tumor types.
L8: Benno Therapeutics is dedicated to changing this. We are developing a new class of immunotherapies based on the iBOOST platform, originally created at Amsterdam UMC, to provide safer and more effective cancer treatments for dogs.
L9: 
L10: A Novel Approach: Targeting Tumor Blood Vessels, Not the Tumor
L11: 
L12: Traditional cancer treatments focus on destroying tumor cells directly. However, cancer cells mutate rapidly, often developing resistance to therapy. Benno Therapeutics takes a fundamentally different approach:
L13: We target the genetically stable blood vessels that tumors need to survive and grow.
L14: 
L15: Our lead candidate, BTX001, is a therapeutic vaccine designed to train the immune system to attack tumor-associated blood vessels. It does this by inducing antibodies against externalized vimentin (eVim)—a self-protein that becomes exposed on the surface of activated endothelial cells in tumor vasculature, but not on healthy tissues.

L6: 田間試驗 受試者招募
L7: 
L8: 一項多中心、隨機分配、開放標籤、雙臂田間試驗以評估PT001治療性疫苗在II-III期口腔惡性黑色素瘤犬隻中的安全性及有效性
L9: 
L10: 試驗標題：
L11: 一項多中心、隨機分配、開放標籤、雙臂田間試驗以評估PT001治療性疫苗在II-III期口腔惡性黑色素瘤犬隻中的安全性及有效性。
L12: 試驗藥物：PT001 (PD-L1及CTLA-4重組蛋白疫苗)
L13: 背景：
L14: 本試驗為一項研究性質的田間試驗，旨在評估研究用試驗藥物（PT001）於腫瘤犬隻中的安全性與有效性。PT001為CTLA-4和PD-L1兩種靶點的重組蛋白疫苗（次蛋白疫苗），利用免疫檢查點（immune-checkpoint）的機制調控免疫反應，為仍在研發階段之研究產品。
L15: 本試驗的目的在於透過受試犬於試驗期間的生理狀況、檢測結果及免疫相關指標的觀察與紀錄，了解此研究產品在腫瘤犬隻中的反應情形，作為後續科學研究與產品開發之參考。

L70: Dilated Cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a disease of heart muscle that results in a decreased ability of the heart to pump blood. L1: # Clinical Trials
L2: 
L3: The medical and surgical diagnostic tests and treatments of animals are similar to those in human medicine. In order to advance knowledge, researchers and clinicians at the College of Veterinary Medicine perform studies that investigate new diagnostics and treatments. These discoveries can often be applied to medicine across all species.
L4: Most clinical trials are based on preliminary laboratory research data that indicate that the new approach is better than what is already available. Benefits to patients in clinical trials include the potential for life-saving therapy when other treatments have failed, lower-cost treatment or diagnostic options, and the advancement of knowledge that will help future patients. Clinical trials are only performed with informed owner consent.

L5: # Gold Nanoparticles - Active Enrollment
L6: 
L7: We are conducting a trial for utilizing gold nanoparticles paired with infrared laser heat. Eligible patients have to have superficial tumors. We are treating the following types:
L8: 
L9: 【4†Image†images.squarespace-cdn.com】
L10: 
L11:   * Dogs with large mast cell tumors (>2 cm)
L12: 
L13:   * Dogs with soft tissue sarcomas (<2cm in diameter)
L14: 
L15:   * Dogs with oral melanoma (2-3cm diameter)
L16: 
L17:   * Dogs with cutaneous or footpad melanoma (<2cm)
L18:   * Cats with oral squamous cell carcinoma not involving the bone
L19: 
L20:   * Cats with other cutaneous tumors like Mast cell tumors, Sarcomas or Carcinomas
L21: 
L22: This clinical trial utilizes gold nanoparticles in a gross disease setting.
L23: Gold Nanoparticles are inert and are given IV to the patient and after a period of time the patient comes back to have the tumor heated with a laser. As the tumor vasculature is heated through the external near infrared spectrum of light, the gold nanoparticles are excited, the laser energy is converted to heat and the tumor vasculature is disrupted killing the tumor from the inside out.

L48: ### Exploratory Field Trial to Investigate Efficacy and Safety of BI 705564 in Dogs with B-cell Lymphoma
L49: 
L50: CURRENTLY ENROLLING
L51: #### SUMMARY OF STUDY:
L52: 
L53: Lymphoma is the most common malignancy in dogs, with B-cell lymphomas accounting for ~70% of all canine lymphomas. There is an unmet need for effective treatments for canine B-cell lymphoma. The standard of care for dogs with B-cell lymphoma provides relatively short median overall survival times despite high remission rates. Side effects are common and may be dose-limiting.

L7: ## What we do
L8: 
L9: CASTR Alliance aims to advance human and veterinary medicine by facilitating the discovery of innovative treatments through the management of high-quality veterinary clinical studies and collaboration with industry leaders and veterinary hospitals.
L10: 
L11: We provide turnkey management of sponsored veterinary clinical studies to pharmaceutical and medical device development teams worldwide.
L12: We partner with state-of-the-art veterinary specialty and referral hospitals throughout the Pacific Northwest and beyond to enroll patients on sponsored clinical studies.
L13: 
L14: We manage sponsored clinical trials that abide by Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards for veterinary studies and are designed to ensure the collection of high-quality data.
L15: We submit all CASTR-run studies for ethical review by an external Veterinary Clinical Studies Committee (VCSC) to prioritize the safety and well-being of all patients.
L16: 
L17: 【4†MORE DETAILS】
L18: ## What motivates us
L19: 
L20: The motivations behind CASTR Alliance’s efforts are to connect companion animals with cutting-edge treatments, address naturally occurring diseases in pets, and accelerate medical innovation for both animals and humans through clinical trials.
L21: 
L22: #### Linking Patients to Caregivers
L23: 
L24: Our sponsored studies link companion animals in need of innovative solutions to novel therapeutic or diagnostic options that may otherwise be unavailable to them.

L2: ENROLLING SOON
L3: # A clinical study for dogs with hemangiosarcoma
L4: 
L5: If your dog has recently been diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, our clinical study at the University of Illinois Veterinary Hospital in Urbana may be an option, and there is no cost to take part. The study is testing FAM-010, a new investigational chemotherapy designed to be gentler on the heart. Your dog may be eligible if they recently had their spleen removed or have surgery scheduled.
L6: 
L7: [Button: Contact the study team]
L8: 【1†Image: A calm dog resting its head on a bed while a person gently pets it.】
L9: ## What is hemangiosarcoma?
L10: 
L11: Hemangiosarcoma is an aggressive cancer that starts in the blood vessels, most often in the spleen. It often shows few signs until a tumor bleeds, so many dogs are diagnosed suddenly, sometimes in an emergency.
L12: 
L13: Treatment usually starts with surgery to remove the spleen, followed by chemotherapy. Even with both, the cancer often comes back, and there is still no FDA-approved treatment for hemangiosarcoma in dogs.

L2: For veterinarians
L3: # Help shape the medicines your patients need next.
L4: 
L5: Familiar is building a new generation of medicines for companion animals, informed by the veterinarians who care for them. Whether you're interested in clinical trials, want to share an unmet need, or simply want to connect with our team, we'd love to hear from you.
L6:

L11: OUR APPROACH
L12: ## Translated from human medicine.
L13: 
L14: Many diseases in dogs and cats share underlying biology with human disease. Familiar starts with drug candidates whose targets and mechanisms are already understood in people, then does the translational work required to determine whether they can become veterinary medicines.

L5: In its first five months, Familiar has built 13 programs for dogs and cats, signed several pharma partnerships, filed a provisional patent and opened two drug development files with FDA CVM.
L6: 
L7: Programs span oncology, neurology, cardiology, respiratory disease, and immunology, with the company's first clinical study set to open at the University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital this fall
L8: 【1†Image: Familiar Therapeutics Launches with $5 Million Seed to Close the Gap Between Human and Veterinary Medicine】
L9: REDWOOD CITY, Calif.: Familiar Therapeutics launched today with $5 million in seed funding to bring the advances of modern human medicine to dogs and cats. The round was led by Pioneer Fund, Icehouse Ventures and BreakTHRU, a syndicate of animal-health industry leaders and veterinarians, with participation from angel investors, including a co-founder of fintech company Robinhood and a founding member of OpenAI and Y Combinator.

L2: # They're family. Their medicine should be familiar.
L3: 
L4: Familiar translates proven human medicines into novel therapeutics for the animals who share our lives, designed to reach every pet, through every veterinary clinic.
L5:

L7: 
L8: The opportunity
L9: ## Our pets get the same diseases we do. They deserve the same breakthroughs.
L10: 
L11: Dogs and cats develop many of the same cancers, immune disorders, and other serious diseases that affect people, but the medicines available to treat them haven’t kept pace. For families and veterinarians, that means facing devastating diagnoses with too few options.
L12: 
L13: We believe pets deserve medicines that can change the course of disease. Familiar exists to help make that possible.

L8: # Oncology Clinical Trials
L9: ## What are clinical trials?
L10: 
L11: Clinical trials are a type of research.  They are an important component of all specialties of medicine and help us as researchers and veterinarians to evaluate new types of diagnostics and treatments.  Clinical trials are variable and may be designed to answer different questions including is a new treatment more effective, is a new diagnostic more specific, or does a new therapy combination have less side effects.
L12: ## Who can join clinical trials?
L13: The Lois Bates Acheson Veterinary Teaching Hospital has many clinical trials underway at any one time.  It is possible that a pet may be eligible for more than one ongoing clinical trial.  There are often initial tests such as a physical exam, blood work and/or imaging that are needed to ensure a patient is approved for enrollment in a trial.  All clinical trials have a unique set of inclusion and exclusion criteria that help the research team enroll the correct patient population.  Your pet’s oncology clinicians will discuss standard treatment and clinical trial treatment options with you.  It is your decision as to whether or not you would like your pet to participate in a clinical trial.

L44: # Veterinary Clinical Trials
L45: 
L46: Clinical trials at VROC help evaluate new cancer treatments for pets by assessing their safety, effectiveness, and potential side effects. Participation is entirely voluntary, and the decision to enroll your pet is yours. However, enrollment in a clinical trial is required for a patient to be seen in our clinic.
L47: Our studies build upon the current standard of care using the same advanced technologies available in leading specialty pet cancer hospitals. While specific outcomes cannot be guaranteed, our team is committed to providing the highest standard of veterinary oncology care throughout each trial.
L48: 
L49: For questions or to learn more about available studies, please contact Paige Neumann, Research Study Coordinator, at 214-645-6221 or by VROC@UTSouthwestern.edu (no-reply@utsouthwestern.edu).
